title: Variables and types
description: Names, dynamic typing, and basic conversions

exercises.title: Declare a binding
exercises.description: Bind `age` to `25` (use `var` or `int`). Print it with `Console.WriteLine`.
hints: Declare an `int` (or use `var` with a numeric literal) for `age`.

exercises.title: Multiple bindings
exercises.description: Bind `name` to `"Rust"` and `version` to `1.85` (double). Print them on one line separated by a space. Use invariant culture so the decimal is always `1.85`.
hints: Use `CultureInfo.InvariantCulture` with `double.ToString` so fractional formatting stays stable.
Interpolate everything with `$"..."` onto one line separated by a space.

exercises.title: Numeric cast
exercises.description: Bind `x` to `100` as `int`. Assign to `double y`. Print `y` so it looks like `100` with no fractional part.
hints: Widen safely with `double y = x` (implicit numeric conversion).
Suppress trailing decimals with format specifier "0" (or "F0") plus invariant culture.

exercises.title: Printing default values
exercises.description: Print `int` zero, `double` zero, an empty string, and `false`, space-separated (same layout as the C#/C# zero-value demo; C# Console.WriteLines `False` with capital F).
hints: Match spacing exactly—the checker expects booleans formatted like False.

exercises.title: Constants
exercises.description: Define constants `MaxScore` and `MinScore` as `100` and `0`. Print both separated by a space.
hints: Use `const` for compile-time `int` constants like scores.
Print both on one line with string interpolation.

exercises.title: Grouped deconstruction
exercises.description: Use tuple deconstruction to bind `host`, `port`, and `debug` from `("localhost", 8080, true)`. Print all three separated by spaces.
hints: Deconstruct with `(string host, int port, bool debug) = (...)`.
Booleans default to Title Case; lowercase with `.ToLowerInvariant()` if stdout must say true/false.

exercises.title: Swap with tuple assignment
exercises.description: Bind `a` and `b` to `5` and `10`. Swap using tuple assignment `(a, b) = (b, a);`. Print `a` and `b` separated by a space.
hints: Tuple swap is `(a, b) = (b, a)` when `a` and `b` are locals.
